title: Root, Layout, and Feature Components knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Root, Layout, and Feature Components”?
options: Root, Layout, and Feature Components means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Root, Layout, and Feature Components removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Root, Layout, and Feature Components should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Root, Layout, and Feature Components helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Root, Layout, and Feature Components helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Root, Layout, and Feature Components is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Application layouts” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Application layouts” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Application layouts” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Application layouts” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Application layouts” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Application layouts” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Application layouts” under Root, Layout, and Feature Components. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Root, Layout, and Feature Components”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
